text: Crate boundary: main.rs is the binary and reaches al_sem only through `pub use`; making is_unused_procedure / the stable-id helper `pub(crate)` does not expose them to it (effective_incoming_count is crate-private too).
evidence: Verified (P14: src/main.rs:17-20, src/lib.rs:19). Design v2 moves the analysis into the library behind one public facade `al_sem::analysis::analyze_project(project, graph: Option<DependencySource>, cfg)`; extract_metrics_ir/object_kind_label move unchanged into analysis.rs; every rule helper stays pub(crate) and shared; main.rs keeps arg plumbing and printers.

text: fan_out: calling the panel's per-routine outgoing selection for every routine rescans the file bucket and ALL ws_event_edges per routine (quadratic). Its semantics (distinct targets vs panel rows, multi-candidate sites, builtins, event links) were undocumented (sol 2, sol 6 second half, opus M2).
evidence: Verified src/lsp/handlers.rs:265-279. Design v2: one pass `handlers::outgoing_targets_by_caller(snap)` over every edges_by_file bucket and ws_event_edges once -> HashMap<caller, HashSet<LspTarget>>. Documented: distinct Routine/Abi targets, not panel rows; every conditional candidate counts; builtin/unresolved never stored; a publisher's subscribers count. Tied to the panel by the test-1 contract against handlers::outgoing on every fixture routine.

text: Cost of the extra snapshot (F4) unmeasured, including default embedded dependencies; the graph should not be built for unchanged text/CSV paths.
evidence: P18 measured (release-fast, Base-App-sized .alpackages, 3 runs + cold HOME): today 0.00 s / 14 MB; snapshot embedded 2.36-2.70 s / 555-571 MB; symbols 1.09-1.19 s / 174-175 MB. Design v2 builds the graph only for --format json (graph: None for text/CSV, which run today's code path at +0). Default source left to the conductor as Q3.

text: Byte-start join between the snapshot and an independent re-read/re-parse can mix source generations; a join that still matches gives wrong graph evidence and F3 never fires.
evidence: Design v2: with a snapshot, rows are built from snap.parsed[rel_posix] (its own AlFile + text) and joined to decls_by_file within that same parse. Re-read+parse only without a snapshot or for a file the snapshot lacks, with null graph fields. F3 rewritten; join-null pinned by test 8.

text: Tests under-discriminate: fan_out dedupe not exercised (no repeated target, opus M1); publisher is raised so R4 untested; framework/interface exclusions and subscribed-unraised InternalEvent unpinned; text keyword absence + CSV header do not prove unchanged output; no degraded or join-null case.
evidence: Fixture v2: Target calls One twice (break -> fan_out 4); unraised unsubscribed IntegrationEvent (R4), subscribed-only InternalEvent (R5), interface + implementation (R6), [Test] + [ConfirmHandler] (R3). Test 6 pins legacy JSON fields, full text and CSV stdout byte-for-byte against frozen outputs minted from the base 84ba2d4b binary. Test 7 no-app.json null case; test 8 join-miss null (hand-stated precondition).

text: routine_id test checked only shape + rerun stability: a wrong object-type label (object_kind_label 'Tableextension' vs ir_object_type 'TableExtension'), guid source, number default or member discriminator would pass. GUID source unnamed.
evidence: P19: `alsem fingerprint <ws> --inventory-only --format json --deterministic` emits stableRoutineId per routine. Test 5 runs CARGO_BIN_EXE_alsem on the same fixture and asserts multiset equality per (objectType, objectNumber, routineName, enclosingMember) for every row; the fixture adds a TableExtension field trigger + procedure and a Page with two OnAction triggers. Helpers stable_object_id_ir (ir_object_type, unwrap_or(0)) and stable_routine_id_ir are shared by l2 and the CLI; GUID = source_text::read_root_app_guid. null for None-typed objects, Interface/ControlAddIn members, nameless routines.

evidence: F2 removed. Design v2: a golden moved by the extraction is investigated as a bug and never licenses a second copy. The pre-existing second composition in engine::snapshot (P20) is recorded as discovery D1, untouched.

evidence: Verified src/main.rs:69-74. Design v2 changes the help to 'With --analyze, used only by --format json (the call-graph fields)'.

text: fan_in is NOT 'exactly the caller groups handlers::incoming returns': the panel drops callers it cannot locate (symbols-only dependency publishers). The grouping loop would also be a second copy (M6).
evidence: Verified P15 (src/lsp/handlers.rs:165-185). The publisher/subscriber asymmetry with the unused rule is documented.

text: The 'lib-side contract test' could not reach the CLI join (run_analysis lives in main.rs), so it would compare the rule with itself.
evidence: Test 2 now lives in tests/cli (links al_sem): runs the binary for JSON and, in the same test, LspSnapshot::build_full + lsp::diagnostics::compute_all on the same fixture; asserts equal (path, line) sets and equality with the literal {NeverCalled}.

text: Unused/fan_in depend on dependency symbols: without .alpackages every subscriber to a dependency event is reported unused and fan_in 0; which dependency source does --analyze use?
evidence: P17 via an LSP stdio driver: the default source is embedded; a Base App OnBeforePostSalesDoc subscriber is not flagged under embedded nor symbols, a misspelled one is flagged under both; with no .alpackages the Base App subscriber IS flagged. Stated in the design + CHANGELOG; asked as Q4 whether CentralGauge workspaces carry .alpackages. No code change.

text: Order of findings[]: unused_procedure entries should be appended after all existing findings so existing entries keep their positions.
evidence: Design v2 states it; test 2 asserts unused findings follow every legacy finding and test 6 compares the legacy findings array byte-for-byte against base.

text: Degraded run (no snapshot) is silent; null semantics undocumented.
evidence: Design v2: one eprintln! warning line (logging is off in JSON mode) naming the null fields; test 7 asserts the stderr line. Round 2 (design-r2): null semantics now stated per field: fan_in/fan_out null = no graph or join miss, never 0; routine_id null without an app id AND, even with a graph, for Interface/ControlAddIn members, unmapped object kinds and nameless routines (independent of graph and join); object_id null when the object has no number; path/access/is_event_subscriber/is_trigger never null. Round 3 (design-r3): the no-graph stderr warning names only fan_in and fan_out as null (plus 'unused procedures are not reported') and makes no claim about routine_id, which is graph-independent; the same wording is used in the code and the CHANGELOG, and test 7 asserts it.
re_raise: sol r2: the blanket 'null means no graph' contradicts intentional null routine_ids for interface/unsupported routines when a graph exists; document per field. sol r3: the no-graph stderr warning still claimed routine_id is null whenever the snapshot cannot be built, contradicting the per-field rules; restrict it to fan_in/fan_out.

text: The issue cites alsem's routineId but the value is stableRoutineId; CHANGELOG must say so and when it changes.
evidence: Round 2 (design-r2) CHANGELOG wording: 'equals alsem's stableRoutineId; it changes when the app id, the object type or number, the routine's name, a parameter type or var, the return type, or (for a member trigger) the enclosing member changes. Matching a changed routine across two versions is left to the consumer.' The object + name join guarantee is removed. Verified the name is hashed: ids::canonical_routine_signature starts with name.to_lowercase() (src/engine/ids.rs). Internal routineId rejected because it hashes the routine kind (P11).
re_raise: sol r2: 'join renamed or re-signatured routines on object + name' fails for renames and cannot separate overloads; remove the guarantee.

text: N1: test 6's frozen text.txt holds `Code Quality Analysis: {project.display()}`; minted with an absolute path in a base worktree it fails in every other checkout, CI and the merge worktree.
evidence: Verified src/main.rs print_text: println!("\nCode Quality Analysis: {}\n", project.display()). Test 6 now mints and runs with cwd = repo root and the same relative `--project tests/fixtures/analyze-json` (cargo runs integration tests with cwd = CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR), so the header is checkout-independent.

text: N2: 'remove keys then compare byte for byte' depends on serde_json preserve_order, which the crate does not request.
evidence: Test 6 compares the stripped current JSON with legacy.json as parsed serde_json::Value, plus a raw-stdout check that each row's first nine keys keep the legacy order and the eight new keys come after quality_score. Text and CSV stay byte-for-byte (no re-serialisation involved).

text: The routine_id test compared multisets per (object, name), so swapping the two OnAction (or Over) ids between rows would pass.
evidence: Test 5 now pins the rows src/A/Util.Codeunit.al:38/42 (Over Integer/Text) and src/D/Card.Page.al:22/28 (OnAction First/Second) to ids computed by hand from engine::ids (normalized_signature_hash + to_stable_routine_id_from_parts). text: Files under a nested app.json got a routine_id minted with the ROOT app's guid, which is not their app.

text: The declaration join did a linear search per routine; distinct callers were counted with a per-routine allocation.
evidence: Per file, one HashMap<start byte, &DeclEntry> (no sortedness assumption, so a map instead of a binary search); one lookup per routine. The caller count keeps the shared incoming_callers helper (the same grouping the panel uses, O(refs) per routine); replacing it with an allocation-free count would split the definition again, so that half is left as is. Proof F11: keying the map by end byte made every join miss and failed tests 1, 2, 8; reverted, pass.

text: The text printer's unused_procedure filter was dead code (text never builds the graph).
evidence: Filter removed; a debug_assert! states that text findings never contain unused_procedure. Proof F12: building the graph for text made the test-6 text run panic on that debug_assert; reverted, pass.

text: JSON --analyze always builds the call graph.
evidence: By design: fan_in/fan_out and unused_procedure need it (Acceptance 1-2). Cost measured and documented (+2.5 s / ~565 MB embedded; --dependency-source symbols about halves it, +1.2 s / 174 MB); text and CSV skip it and are byte-identical to base (test 6). No new flag now.
